title: Backpacking in Grayson Highlands State Park
description:
Asheville Adventures 30’s & 40’s
Join me for a 2.5-day backpacking trip through the Grayson Highlands, where we will get to experience incredible mountain views, spectacular sunsets, wildflowers, majestic forests, and maybe even some wild ponies!

This backpacking trip will begin *at the trailhead* at 10 am on Friday, April 17th, and we will plan to finish before midday on Sunday.

I have created a custom route with the link below.

https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/custom-route-mount-rogers-loop-trail-53bd310?u=i&sh=p0nozs

Day 1: We will depart the trailhead at 10am, hiking about 10 miles and just under 1,700 ft elevation.
Day 2: We will begin our day early-to-mid morning, and hike 12 miles and almost 2,800 ft.
Day 3: Sunday morning, we will have just under 3 miles on mostly flat terrain to reach the trailhead, with enough energy for the drive home!

Total distance for the 2.5 days will be just under 25 miles and 4,500 ft vertical elevation gain. While this is not specifically geared towards beginner backpackers, I want all to feel welcome. If I haven't hiked or backpacked with you before, please feel free to still RSVP and I can reach out to you directly to review your experience and answer any questions!

There is a fee of $15 per vehicle to park in the overnight backpacking lot. Please book your permit in advance using the link below!
https://www.reservevaparks.com/Web/#!park/11

Below are a few housekeeping items that you must read in order to participate.

1\. You must come prepared with all of your own gear for overnight backpacking\, including enough food for 2\.5 days\, enough water \(or the ability to filter water\)\, navigation\, and the ability to make it back to the trailhead on your own if separated\, etc\.
2\. I am not a certified guide\, nor will I be acting as the hiking guide for this trip\. This is a social outing\, everyone will be responsible for their own navigation\, gear\, essentials\, etc\. My goal is obviously to keep everyone safe\, together\, and having a good time\, but I cannot guarantee anyone's safety\. By RSVPing "yes" to this event\, you are releasing me from any\-and\-all liability should you experience illness\, injury\, or worse during \(or as a result of\) this trip\.
3\. This trail is dog\-friendly and you are welcome to bring your dog IF you can guarantee that they will be kept on a leash AT ALL TIMES\. Zero exceptions\.
4\. Please brush up on your Leave No Trace Principles \- https://www\.nps\.gov/articles/leave\-no\-trace\-seven\-principles\.htm
5\. There are bears in the park\, so bring a bear canister\. While there are some sites with bear boxes\, they are not guaranteed\. It is also not guaranteed that there will be trees to hang a bear bag\, so bear canisters are recommended\.

This event has a short RSVP deadline because of required permits. If you don't make an RSVP before the cutoff, please message me and I can check for availability of permits :-)

This will be an amazing trail, can't wait to share it with all of you!

title: Nature Journaling
description:
Nature Journaling
with Andrew Dundas 
Friday, April 17  |  10 – 12pm 
BRN – Elective  |  BREG – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
Nature journaling fosters a connection to the outdoors unique to each individual who pursues it. It can be a means to practice art or poetry, a therapeutic moment of reflection, or scientific exploration of the ecosystems around us. Join arboretum staff in a review of the principles of nature journaling, exploration of other’s work, and visits to multiple sites across the Arboretum with optional prompts and tips for journaling. Basic supplies will be provided, such as notebooks and writing/drawing utensils, but you are also welcome to bring your own.  
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time.  
Andrew Dundas is an Adult Education employee with a passion for history, folklore, writing, and nature. He studied journalism and visual storytelling at the University of Chapel Hill before joining the Arboretum’s Youth Education Department and later the Adult Education Department.

title: Spare-Time Gardening
description:
Spare-Time Gardening
with Martha Rollefson 
Friday, April 17  |  10 – 12pm 
BRN – Elective | BREG – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
Here’s a 2-hour crash course on making the most of the spare time you have for working in your garden.  I’ll share tricks learned & practices developed during more than 40 years of squeezing garden work into an otherwise busy life.  I sum it up with these principles: 1) Choose Wisely… 2) Pace Yourself for the Essential Chores… 3) Pluck it up! … 4) Don’t Shoot Yourself in the Foot! … and 5) Celebrate!  Even experienced gardeners will probably get some new ideas for making their garden chores less strenuous and more impactful. You will also receive a garden assessment tool that will help you articulate your vision for your own garden in a way that will guide your efforts. 
Martha Rollefson has been a spare-time gardener for decades who got the “wildlife habitat” bug over 20 years ago. After leaving the corporate world she started working at Wild Birds Unlimited “to support her gardening habit,” and she joined the Western Carolina Botany Club to learn more about native plants. While feeding the birds and observing how gardening and wildlife interact, she has developed numerous techniques for saving time and money while reducing her carbon footprint. She lives next to the Etowah Valley Golf Resort with her husband David and mini-doxie, Eva.

title: Intro to WNC Invasive Plant ID
description:
Intro to WNC Invasive Plant ID
with Erin Canter 
Friday, April 17  |  1 – 3:30pm 
BRN – Elective |  BREG – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
In this beginners’ course, participants will learn strategies for plant ID and use them to identify plants that are invasive to Western North Carolina. We’ll discuss the impact of invasive plants and other invasive species, and introduce strategies for their management and control in our own properties and public spaces. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Erin Canter is a Southern Appalachian Naturalist who specializes in southeastern ecology. She worked as the Manager of Science Literacy and Research at a nonprofit education center in the Great Smoky Mountains, working with all ages to explore their bioregion through science and hands-on exploration, before moving to this side of the mountains in early 2024. She now works at American Conservation Experience here in WNC, helping young people begin their conservation careers through applied conservation projects in the region.

title: Official Downtown After 5 After Party: Saving Shirley + Aden Webb
location: Fitz and the Wolfe, 1 Battery Park Ave, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Some bands play songs. Saving Shirley throws a full-blown party.
Born in the mountains of Western North Carolina, this high-energy crew has built a reputation for turning rooms upside down with a setlist packed with pop, rock, and dance anthems from the 90s through the 2010s. Think Green Day, The Killers, Blink-182, Rihanna, Bruno Mars, and plenty more. One minute the crowd is belting out Mr. Brightside, the next the dance floor is packed and nobody remembers where they left their drink.
Singalongs, call-and-response chaos, and the kind of energy that pulls people out of their seats and up to the stage. It is less of a concert and more of a “how did it get this wild in here” kind of night.


Saving Shirley runs from 8pm to 11pm. Grab a cocktail, keep the Downtown After 5 momentum going, and don’t call it a night just yet.

From 11pm to 1am, Chris Vita takes it late with an acoustic set that trades the chaos for something a little more dialed-in. A Nashville-based singer-songwriter with roots in South Carolina, Chris brings a mix of country influence and heartfelt storytelling shaped by years of writing and performing in Music City. The kind of set where you actually feel the songs.
Two vibes, one night. Start loud, end strong

The music fills the space like a second heartbeat, sometimes rowdy, sometimes intimate, always memorable. It’s not background noise. It’s the reason you’re here. fitzandthewolfe.com

title: Wild Flower #2 - Cat Gap John Rock
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
We will meet at the Fish Hatchery / Pisgah Center for Wildlife Education. We will hike clockwise up the Cat Gap Loop to the John Rock trail.

There should be nice wildflowers this time of year, although it has been a dry spring.

We will hike up to John Rock, stop for a snack and social chatting, and then continue around the loop to the junction with Cat Gap trail.

Rating: Strenuous but doable
Distance: 5.5 miles
Elevation: 1,000 feet
Surface: Trail
Pace: 3 mph on the flats, 2.5 mph up John Rock
Gear: water, snack, poles.
Features: River, view of Looking Glass Rock, Ravens.
Dogs: On leash
Route: [Cat Gap Trail](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/cat-gap-trail-to-john-rock-loop-2b515e2--2?p=-1&sh=ifwm3x&utm_medium=map_share&utm_source=alltrails_virality) to John Rock Loop on AllTrails

title: Ecology of the Native Azalea Collection Walk
description:
Ecology of the Native Azalea Collection Walk
with Lauren Lampley 
Saturday, April 18 | 9 – 10:30 am 
BRN – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
For Native Azalea Day, join Adult Education Coordinator, Lauren Lampley, on an ecology walk through the Native Azalea Collection highlighting different plants, wildlife, and ecosystems found within the collection. We will also discuss how the different wetlands and creeks play into the ecology of the space and how our Community Science Projects make use of the unique space for science. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

location: 310 ART at Re Imagine Studio, 15 Spivey Lake Drive, Fairview, NC, 28730, United States
description:
$165.00
Saturday, April 18th – 10 AM to 4 PM- $165 – All materials supplied! 
If you’ve ever watched those hypnotic fluid‑acrylic videos and thought, I want to feel that magic, this workshop is your chance to dive in—literally and creatively. Expect to feel mesmerized, loosened up, and totally absorbed as you watch color swirl, stretch, and dance across your canvas. This is the kind of class where you lose track of time in the best possible way. 
You’ll experience the joy of letting paint move with you instead of fighting against you, discovering how different mediums, consistencies, and techniques create wildly different effects. Instead of frustration or muddy results, you’ll feel that satisfying “ohhh, that’s how it works” click as everything starts to flow. With plenty of demos, hands‑on experimenting, and space to play, you’ll leave with pieces that feel alive—and uniquely yours. 
It’s a relaxed, creative, slightly addictive kind of day, complete with a lunch break to recharge and admire your works‑in‑progress. All materials are included; all you need to bring is your curiosity (and a snack). 
This class seats 8 students. For any questions regarding our cancellation or transfer policy, please refer to the link in our navigation bar. 
Robyn Crawford studied at Emerson College, Massachusetts College of Art, and Rochester Institute of Technology’s School of Photographic Arts and Sciences. She has been a mixed media artist, photographer, teacher, and creativity coach for over 30 years and has exhibited work throughout the Carolinas.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Native Azalea Day
location: Native Azalea Collection
description:
Native Azalea Day
April 18, 2026
10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.
Visit the gardens this spring for Native Azalea Day, an invitation to celebrate and experience azaleas through the eyes of plant enthusiasts, botanists, and artists. For one day only, visitors can observe as plein air artists capture the scene in paint and pen, learn about the garden and its collection on a walking tour, and participate in hands-on activities for children and adults. 
A shuttle to the Collection will be available between 10:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., departing to and from the Baker Visitor Center throughout the event. Visitors are also welcome to walk to the Native Azalea Collection from the Gatehouse Parking Lot using Old Mill Road to Bent Creek Road, or can park at the Baker Visitor Center and walk down Running Cedar Road to Bent Creek Road. Walkers should be prepared to travel one mile over unpaved roads and paths. 
Special thanks to Community Partner Carolina Native Nursery for sponsoring Native Azalea Day.

title: Adult Studio: Plein Air Watercolor + Gouache
location: NC
description:
TWO DAY STUDIO — Saturdays April 18 and April 25. 
Have you ever wanted to paint en plein air? Join us for a two-day workshop where we’ll explore light and color on location using watercolor and gouache. Inspired by American Impressionism, this class will guide participants through creating an expressive and vibrant landscape painting, emphasizing emotion and light over technique. If you’ve ever been intimidated by painting, this class will help you tap into greater creative freedom and boldness. We’ll start on location at the North Carolina Arboretum on day 1, and finish in the Studio on day 2. NC Arboretum entry will be required; carpool options will be arranged to reduce cost. All skill levels are welcome. The instruction will be tailored to your experience level and willingness to challenge yourself. All materials will be provided. 
Yekaterina Benson is an Asheville-based landscape painter, hiking the Blue Ridge Mountains and capturing their beauty. Her paintings are emotionscapes: visual depictions of what we experience in places that make us feel awe, joy, aliveness, inspiration, or peace. Her work explores the full range between expressive and realistic, and strives to capture colors that may not be visible, but are felt. Yekaterina’s art celebrates the unique landscapes of Western North Carolina and highlights treasured local spots such as waterfalls, overlooks, trails, and mountain peaks.

title: Feminine and the Clay Figure, with local artist Katie Croft
location: ArtPlay Studio, 53 Orange Street, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
Join us for an afternoon of working with your hands, clay and your imagination as we explore our relationship to ancient female figurines with Katie’s thoughtful guidance. 
In this class, Katie will introduce us to the realm of experimental archaeology, using clay as a way to explore the meaning and possible uses of historical Venus Figurines. These figurines appear across many ancient cultures—images of voluptuous female bodies without identifying facial features, repeated again and again throughout antiquity. While their exact purpose remains unknown, their presence has endured, inviting curiosity, reverence, and inquiry. 
Through hands-on making, we will explore the how and why of these objects, employing experimental archaeology as a way of learning through embodied practice. 
Participants will build their own female figurines, guided by personal intention and informed by culture of origin, family lineage, and individual needs, hopes, and desires. Throughout the process, we will reflect together on why we made these objects, how they might be used, and how they may continue to influence our lives beyond the workshop. 
We will work with materials of the ancient makers, meaning we will be making our figures from clay. There is no experience with clay necessary as within each of you the knowledge already exists to create these figures as your ancestors did.

title: Body Process Class: Restoration of Communion with Earth
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
## What If Your Body Has Been Waiting for This?

## **You’re Invited: Access Consciousness Body Process Class**

What if your body isn’t something to fix…
but something to listen to?

What if it has been whispering (or maybe shouting) for your attention in ways you were never taught to understand?

I’d love to invite you to a beautiful, hands-on **Access Consciousness Body Process class** — a space where you get to receive, gift, and explore a different communion with bodies.

### What Is a Body Process?

Access Consciousness Body Processes are gentle, hands-on techniques that invite the body to:
• Release stored trauma and shock
• Activate natural capacities
• Undo limitations held in tissue and cellular memory
• Restore communication between you and your body

This isn’t massage.
It isn’t energy work in the traditional sense.
It’s a conversation — with the body.
And bodies respond.

### In This Class You Will:

✨ Learn a specific Access Body Process you can use for life
✨ Both gift and receive the process (yes, you get sessions too!)
✨ Explore how judgment impacts the body
✨ Discover new tools for ease, vitality, and awareness
✨ Leave certified to practice this body process on others

No prior experience is required. Just a body. And a willingness.

### What Becomes Possible?

Many people report:
• Increased ease in chronic patterns
• Greater relaxation and presence
• Changes in long-held physical limitations
• A deeper sense of trust with their body

But more than anything — possibility.
What if your body has capacities you’ve never been shown how to access?

If you’ve been asking for more ease, more connection, more *aliveness* — this may be the invitation your body has been waiting for.

Would your body enjoy this?

location: ArtPlay Studio, 53 Orange Street, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
Join us for a Sunday afternoon of community and creativity as we explore the versatile—and very fun—medium of alcohol inks! 
In this beginner-friendly class, you’ll discover how alcohol inks interact with one another as they bloom, expand, and flow across the surface, creating unexpected forms and organic movement. Working on black synthetic paper, we’ll experience how beautifully the inks reveal themselves in vibrant contrast against dark backgrounds. 
Throughout the class, Kimberly will share techniques for creating floral/petal forms and compositions, creating soft fades, layering for richness and dimension, and adding luminous metallic accents that bring your work to life. You’ll learn how to gently guide the movement of the inks using air and simple tools, allowing the natural interplay of colors to create depth, motion, and delightful surprises along the way. 
All materials are provided, and no prior experience is needed—just curiosity and a willingness to play!

title: Pre-Event Picnic - Olivette Riverside Concert
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
*What could be better than a Sunday afternoon of connecting, socializing, and listening to great music with fellow Nomads at an outdoor concert by the beautiful French Broad River?*

**What:** Pre-Concert Social
**Where:** The Lawn - Olivette Riverside Pavilion
**Artists:** GOLDPINE
**When:** 3pm on Sunday, April 19th
**To Bring:** BYOB & BYOC (chair) + sharable food

**Details**
Join fellow music-loving Nomads for a pre-concert picnic on the lawn by the Olivette Riverside Pavilion. Use [this link](https://www.chatthillsmusic.com/goldpine) to purchase tickets to the GOLDPINE concert on Sunday, April 19th. Nomads attending the concert are invited to bring shareable snacks and appetizers, along with your beverages of choice.

This informal Nomads gathering starts at 3pm. Live music from GOLDPINE will be from 4 - 6pm.

Bring comfortable folding chairs and/or blankets for picnicking on the lawn. It you want to sit in the Pavilion for the concert, you will need your own chair.

**The Music**
Chatt Hills welcomes GOLDPINE for the first event in their 2026 "[Sundays by the River](https://www.chatthillsmusic.com/all-shows)" concert series. Fans of contemporary Americana will love this folksy and energetic husband-wife duo. Pairing award-winning songwriting with strong vocals and harmony, Nashville-based GOLDPINE presents engaging stories about life, love and the human experience.
To sample what is in store from Ben and Kassie, check out [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hri3PoSysDM).

**Tickets**
We highly recommend purchasing your tickets in advance. Tickets are $25 each ($30.52, including fees) -- and kids are free! Well-behaved dogs are also welcome.

[Tickets and more info](https://www.chatthillsmusic.com/goldpine).

**Directions**
Olivette is just 15 minutes from downtown Asheville. Click [this link](https://maps.app.goo.gl/rnqGwUiLLJghxo1r8) to get directions directly to the parking area for the Pavilion. Otherwise, use the address below to get to Olivette and follow the Chatt Hills event signs to the Pavilion.
Carpooling is encouraged.

**Chatt Hills Music**
Chatt Hills Music is an independent non-profit organization dedicated to enriching communities through the power of live music. Chatt Hills brings an eclectic lineup of award-winning artists to Asheville and the surrounding region. From Americana and singer-songwriters to jazz, rock, and classical, every concert offers a unique musical experience.
This outdoor concert series takes place just minutes from downtown Asheville at the scenic Olivette Riverside Pavilion, located along the banks of the French Broad River—where great music meets beautiful views.
World-class music, scenic views, affordable tickets — and kids are always free.

**The Venue**
Olivette is a 411-acre planned community and historic farm, located along the French Broad River, just 6.7 miles from downtown Asheville. An agrihood community, Olivette is home to a vibrant vegetable, fruit and flower farm. With 1.3 miles of river frontage, the community has a seven acre riverfront park with a pavilion, miles of walking trails, community gardens, a dog park, and multiple neighborhood gathering spaces.

title: Fresh Market toward visitor's Center
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
We will meet near the Fresh Market on Highway 25 and walk 2.5 miles in on the MTS trail and then back to the Fresh Market. This trail comes out on the road at least twice, so keep this in mind with dogs on the trail.

This is a fairlly easy hike, and we go at a high average to low advanced speed, which is roughly about 3.0 to 3.2 mph. There are no super long hills. It's pretty undulating all the way. The biggest hill is at the beginning.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park closest to the forest on the side where Haywood Appliance is.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Explorer Loop - MST - South Ridge Loop - 6.6 Miles 1300+ Ft
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Details**

* 6.6 Miles, 1300 Ft elevation gain with option to add 300 more ft
* Carpool meeting time is 9:15 at the Asheville Outlets parking lot behind the Waffle House.
* Sign up starts Friday at 5pm

This is a nice Bent Creek loop starting at the Explorer Loop trailhead and going up to the MST by Chestnut Cove. We will head down the MST beyond Sleepy Gap and drop back into Bent Creek on a no-name trail and back along South Ridge and Explorer Loop to the trailhead. There is an option just after Chestnut Cove to go up to Grassy Knob and gain about another 300 ft of elevation. We will do a moderate pace of about 2.7 mph but stop for breaks as needed.

It looks like the cooler weather is returning next week but I am going to do a bit of an easier one on Monday. I am substitute leading the fitness group hike on Wednesday so that will be my harder hike for the week.

**CARPOOL**
We will meet at the Asheville Outlets behind the Waffle House at 9:15. Please be there a little early so we can leave at 9:15 for the trailhead. Parking is limited at the Explorer Loop trailhead so please try to carpool.

**WEATHER**
I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:30 AM if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
You can message me through MeetUp until 9:00 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: (508) 965-2333.

title: Coworking day: Bankers Hours in Marshall
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Join us for a focused and relaxed coworking day at Bankers Hours, a beautifully restored historic space in the heart of Marshall, North Carolina.

Nestled in a quiet mountain town just outside Asheville, Marshall offers a refreshing change of pace—think walkable streets, charming cafes, and a peaceful riverside atmosphere that makes it easy to settle into deep work. Bankers Hours itself carries that same energy, blending old-world character with a warm, functional workspace that feels both inspiring and unpretentious.

We’ll gather from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM on April 21 for a full day of independent work alongside a small group of like-minded professionals. With attendance capped at 15 people, the environment stays focused, comfortable, and conducive to real productivity.

If the weather cooperates, we’ll have access to the rooftop patio—a quiet favorite for reading, thinking, or getting some sun while you work. It’s one of those rare spots that makes you want to slow down just enough to do your best thinking.
Marshall has several nearby restaurants and cafes within easy walking distance, making lunch breaks simple and enjoyable.

Parking note: The bank lot may fill up, but additional public parking is available throughout town just a short walk away.
Whether you’re looking to make progress on a big project or just want a change of scenery, this coworking day offers a calm, intentional setting to get things done.

We might just take a walk to a brewery down the street at 4pm!

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Ukrainian Pysanky Easter egg workshop
location: Studio A
description:
Pysanky are a lot like Asheville- unique, fun and colorful!



In this workshop we will be making beautiful Ukrainian Easter eggs – pysanky. You will learn the method of batik – also called wax-resist – dying. You will also be familiarized with the wide range of Ukrainian folk art traditional patterns, designs and symbols and their history. The designs are made with beeswax which is melted in the flame of a candle and applied to the egg using a tool called a kistka. The eggs are dipped into successively darker dyes. At the end of the process the beeswax is melted off to reveal the beautiful and colorful design. You may use the traditional patterns, or also freestyle and make up your own design. Pysanky are fun, relaxing, and meditative to create. And, the symbols are all good wishes, so it is always the perfect time to create eggs with symbols wishing for good health, long life, strength and protection and other good things. 



$75 per person (cash/check) or $78 (credit card) includes use of all supplies. Please contact me for more information or to sign up! $10 discount for WNC residents – mention code: WNC2026.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Shut Up & Write!

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

description:
Spring Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum
with Lauren Lampley 
Thursday, April 23  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
Interested in learning how to identify wildflowers? Join Lauren on this walk around the Arboretum property where we will go over different ways of identifying plants and different families of flowers. Some flowers are very difficult to identify to species and some are relatively easy so we will talk about how to get as close as possible with tools we can easily carry into the field. We will be using Newcomb’s guide to key out some of the less common flowers but will focus on learning how to look closely at flowers in order to identify them. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

title: Ukrainian Pysanky Easter egg workshop
location: Studio A
description:
Pysanky are a lot like Asheville- unique, fun and colorful!



In this workshop we will be making beautiful Ukrainian Easter eggs – pysanky. You will learn the method of batik – also called wax-resist – dying. You will also be familiarized with the wide range of Ukrainian folk art traditional patterns, designs and symbols and their history. The designs are made with beeswax which is melted in the flame of a candle and applied to the egg using a tool called a kistka. The eggs are dipped into successively darker dyes. At the end of the process the beeswax is melted off to reveal the beautiful and colorful design. You may use the traditional patterns, or also freestyle and make up your own design. Pysanky are fun, relaxing, and meditative to create. And, the symbols are all good wishes, so it is always the perfect time to create eggs with symbols wishing for good health, long life, strength and protection and other good things. 



$75 per person (cash/check) or $78 (credit card) includes use of all supplies. Please contact me for more information or to sign up! $10 discount for WNC residents – mention code: WNC2026. 
Full schedule at https://www.ashevillestudioa.com/workshops or contact me to if you’d like to request a different date! 
Email andreakulish [at] gmail dot com or call/text 828 423 6459 to sign up or for more info!

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. title: Fresh Market toward visitor's Center
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
We will meet near the Fresh Market on Highway 25 and walk 2.5 miles in on the MTS trail and then back to the Fresh Market. This trail comes out on the road at least twice, so keep this in mind with dogs on the trail.

This is a fairlly easy hike, and we go at a high average to low advanced speed, which is roughly about 3.0 to 3.2 mph. There are no super long hills. It's pretty undulating all the way. The biggest hill is at the beginning.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park closest to the forest on the side where Haywood Appliance is.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Walking Meditation & Qigong
description:
Walking Meditation & Qigong
with Jenne Sluder 
Friday, April 24  |  9 – 10am 
REGISTER HERE 
Enjoy a slow, mindful walking meditation through the gardens, practicing breath awareness and sensory attention to touch the deep peace and simple wonders of quiet time in nature. This session begins with a series of gentle and easy Qigong movements to clear the mind, release tension, support the body and brain’s natural healing processes, and generate a sense of inner calm. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

title: Geology of the Blue Ridge Field Class
description:
Geology of the Blue Ridge Field Class
with Anton DuMars 
Friday, April 24 | Meet in Brevard at 12, class time is 12 – 4 pm 
BRN – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
On this Field Experience, we will observe and interpret evidence of Appalachian mountain-building events. Participants can put their hands on a 380+/- million-year-old pluton and observe their post-uplift weathering, jointing, and exfoliation. In addition, participants observe and interpret river processes, transport, and depositional environments of sediments derived from up-gradient sources. The experience includes on-site geologic map reading and interpretation. 
This off-site program has stops in the Pisgah Forest near Brevard NC along The Pisgah Highway including Daniel Ridge and the Davidson River. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy to moderate trails. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Anton DuMars, a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. Ideally, he’s spending time on a hiking trail or aboard his sailboat.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

description:
Mountain Science Expo 2026
April 25, 2026
10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.
Join us for a free STEM-oriented science festival where you can interact with scientists, explore nature, and grow your curiosity! 
The Mountain Science Expo is a part of the larger NC Science Festival, a state-wide and month-long event dedicated to celebrating the impact of science educationally, culturally, and economically on our state. The NC Science Festival and the Mountain Science Expo hope to inspire children to pursue—and adults to support—the sciences, such that North Carolina can lead the country and the world as a place of innovation and learning.  
The Expo will feature live animal presentations, exhibitors from across the region, special interactive activities, and more! It takes place in both of The North Carolina Arboretum’s main buildings and through the gardens. 
Rain or shine, the Mountain Science Expo takes place fully within indoor or covered spaces at The Arboretum! 
Special thanks to Community Partners AvL Technologies, RTI International, and Everyday Gourmet for sponsoring Mountain Science Expo. 
Exhibitors
The Mountain Science Expo provides an opportunity for all ages to learn about STEM fields and  interact with scientists and science educators in a hands-on and wonder-filled environment. Past exhibitors include: 

Asheville Makers
Asheville Museum of Science
Muddy Sneakers
The National Center for Environmental Information (NCEI)
The North Carolina Department of Air Quality (NCDAQ)
UNCA STEAM Labs
RiverLink
Blue Ridge Audubon Chapter
FIND Outdoors
And more!

Golden Tickets
Kids can get special Golden Tickets! Simply check out a science book from your local library, and you’ll receive a Golden Ticket good for free parking the day of the event. Participating County Libraries: Buncombe, Henderson, Transylvania, Haywood, Madison, McDowell, Rutherford 
There is no additional cost to attend Mountain Science Expo beyond our standard parking fee. As always, Arboretum Society members and their accompanying guests can enter for FREE (guests must be in member vehicles to receive free entry). 
This event is part of Spring Into the Arb! Celebrate the return of spring with a series of events and happenings throughout March, April, May and June! Spring is a time of renewal and emergence, and The North Carolina Arboretum is excited to welcome this season with plant shows, nature programs, education, music, art and more!

Come, join me in this adventure. Let us create together, stitching hope and beauty into every piece. May this class be a wellspring of inspiration, a gentle reminder of our own resilience, and a celebration of the quiet power of renewal.
I look forward to seeing what you will create, and to sharing in the comfort and peace that art can bring.

description:
TWO DAY STUDIO — Saturdays April 18 and April 25. 
Have you ever wanted to paint en plein air? Join us for a two-day workshop where we’ll explore light and color on location using watercolor and gouache. Inspired by American Impressionism, this class will guide participants through creating an expressive and vibrant landscape painting, emphasizing emotion and light over technique. If you’ve ever been intimidated by painting, this class will help you tap into greater creative freedom and boldness. We’ll start on location at the North Carolina Arboretum on day 1, and finish in the Studio on day 2. NC Arboretum entry will be required; carpool options will be arranged to reduce cost. All skill levels are welcome. The instruction will be tailored to your experience level and willingness to challenge yourself. All materials will be provided. 
Yekaterina Benson is an Asheville-based landscape painter, hiking the Blue Ridge Mountains and capturing their beauty. Her paintings are emotionscapes: visual depictions of what we experience in places that make us feel awe, joy, aliveness, inspiration, or peace. Her work explores the full range between expressive and realistic, and strives to capture colors that may not be visible, but are felt. Yekaterina’s art celebrates the unique landscapes of Western North Carolina and highlights treasured local spots such as waterfalls, overlooks, trails, and mountain peaks.

title: Interest List: Mindful Speed Dating Event 55+
description:
Mindful Meet & Mingle – Asheville Singles
**This is an application-based event.**
**RSVP on Meetup does not mean that you have register for this event.**

Participation requires completing a short interest form and receiving a private registration link. This is paid event. Please do not make travel plans or assume attendance until you receive a confirmation email.

https://forms.gle/UiMjc9CwpPr9Wipa9

About Event
Meet in the Moment is a guided, speed-dating style experience for conscious singles who want to slow down, drop out of small talk, and connect with presence and authenticity.
This is not traditional speed dating. There is no pressure to perform, impress, or decide anything in the moment. Instead, you’ll be gently guided into embodied connection through simple mindfulness prompts, structured one-on-one conversations, and moments of reflection.
The intention is to help you feel grounded, relaxed, and real while meeting others who value emotional availability, curiosity, and meaningful connection.

What to Expect

* A short opening grounding practice to help you arrive and settle
* A series of timed, one-on-one conversations with gentle prompts
* Clear structure so you can relax and be yourself
* Space to reflect and notice how connection feels in your body
* A warm, inclusive, and respectful environment

You do not need dating experience, meditation experience, or confidence in small talk. Just come as you are.

Who is this for

* Singles who want deeper connection, not surface-level chatting
* People who value mindfulness, emotional awareness, and authenticity
* Those curious about meeting others in a slower, more intentional way
* Anyone feeling tired of dating apps or conventional speed dating

Important Notes

* This event is designed for people who are emotionally available and open to respectful connection
* You will never be asked to share anything you’re uncomfortable sharing
* Attraction is welcome, but there is no expectation to match or follow up

Ticketing & Balance

To support a balanced experience, tickets are offered by gender and capped to keep numbers even. If one ticket type sells out, you may join the waitlist.

We run the event **every other month** with alternating age ranges: 35–54 and 55–74. Choose the session that aligns with your life stage.

With first-hand testimony from the artist himself on the eve of his mysterious disappearance, this film reveals Caravaggio as never before. Featuring masterpiece after masterpiece and testimony from leading experts from around the world, Caravaggio immerses audiences in the hidden narratives of the artist’s life, piecing together clues embedded within his incredible art. 
Caravaggio’s masterpieces are some of art’s most instantly recognisable. No one else uses his signature blend of dramatic light, intense naturalism and bold, striking figures. His astonishing paintings have captivated audiences for centuries. But there lies a deeper mystery – one that still beckons us to explore. What do these masterpieces reveal about the man behind the brush? The intriguing self-depictions within his works – sometimes disguised, sometimes in plain sight – offer a rare window into his psyche and personal struggles. Join us as we unravel the story of one of history’s most brilliant, complex and controversial figures. Co-Directed by David Bickerstaff & Phil Grabsky. Runtime 100 minutes.

title: April 26th Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/april-26th-community-cuddles)**[Click HERE to register!](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/april-26th-community-cuddles)**

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**
1\. Clothes stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\.
4\. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with\.
5\. Speak up if you have a question\, concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. All emotions are welcome\- we love vulnerability\.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.
* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Spring Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
description:
Spring Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
with Jenne Sluder 
Tuesday, April 28  |  10 am – 4pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Set aside a day for quiet reflection and renewal at the North Carolina Arboretum, centering themes from the poetry of Mary Oliver. Calm your mind, refresh your spirit, and relax your body and nervous system with a gentle immersion into mind-body centering practices both indoors and in nature. Expect slow, mindful yoga and qigong, guided meditation, progressive relaxation + sound bath, contemplative readings from Mary Oliver, and time for personal journaling and quiet time in nature. All mind-body practices will be gentle and accessible, including the choice to do any seated movements or meditations in a chair or on a cushion according to your own body’s needs. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

title: Artist Talk with Karen Sixkiller: Cherokee Water Beetle Brings Sacred Earth to North Carolina
description:
Artist Talk with Karen Sixkiller: Cherokee Water Beetle Brings Sacred Earth to North Carolina
with Karen Sixkiller 
Tuesday, April 28  |  5:30 – 7 pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Learn about how one of the oldest Cherokee stories inspired Artist Karen Sixkiller to create the new ‘Sacred Earth’ sculptural installation at The North Carolina Arboretum.  Sixkiller explores the aspects of magical realism and symbolism that combine her larger-than-life water beetle with the faceted geometric “mud” he perches on. Follow the technical journey of Karen Sixkiller’s simple clay maquette through the process of becoming a large bronze piece of public art. 
Karen Sixkiller is a contemporary sculptor residing on the Olympic Peninsula of Washington state. Sixkiller creates sculptures using metal, ceramic, glass beads, leather/suede and fabric. As a Cherokee Nation citizen much of her work is informed by Native American understandings or stories. Cherokee Nation has purchased many of Karen Sixkiller’s ceramic and mixed media sculptural pieces for display in official buildings. She has permanent public art installations in Tahlequah OK, Olympia and Port Angeles WA, and now Asheville NC; as well as several temporary installations in Coeur d’Alene ID, Olympia WA and Lake Oswego OR. Her work has been featured at multiple Indigenous and non-Indigenous art shows.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Shut Up & Write!

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

Join Dan Lazar on this walk and talk designed to point out signs of life awakening in springtime. Wildflowers are blooming, amphibians are mating, and birds are returning to their nesting habitats. Opportunities for learning in place are far from dormant in this or any season at the Arboretum!

Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

title: Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons
description:
Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons
with Carlton Burke 
Thursday, April 30  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
Since birds are capable of long distance flights and many engage in annual migration rituals, their presence in our area often changes in relation to the seasons of the year.  In this class we will discuss the seasonal patterns of southern Appalachian birds and focus on some of the major species and their annual life cycles. As part of this program, there will be a “lab” portion where students will be able to meet some live birds and participate in other hands-on components to deepen the learning. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: Volunteer opportunity @ Manna Food Bank
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
## **AVL Digital Nomads Volunteer Day at MANNA FoodBank**

## **Hunger hides in plain sight in Asheville and surrounding communities.**

Many of our neighbors are struggling in silence — facing empty shelves and impossible choices.
Let’s show up and do something about it.
Join **AVL Digital Nomads** for a volunteer shift at **MANNA FoodBank**, where we’ll work together to:

* Sort donations
* Bag bulk food items
* Date-check perishable goods
* Support the team keeping our community fed

Together, we can help create a more caring Asheville where no one goes without a meal.

***

## **What to Expect**

If it’s your first time volunteering at MANNA, here’s a quick walkthrough:

* Plan to arrive a few minutes early at the former FedEx warehouse
* Turn left into the **volunteer parking lot**
* Walk past the turnstile fence and enter the warehouse
* Continue down the hallway past the bathrooms and fridges
* You’ll find a small lounge area with high-top tables where volunteers gather

MANNA staff will usually greet you somewhere between the parking lot and the lounge.
There will be individual volunteers in addition to our group, so:

* Look for other **AVL Digital Nomads**
* Introduce yourself and connect with new arrivals
* We’ll coordinate with simple name tags

Once everyone is checked in:

* MANNA staff will give a **brief safety overview**
* Then assign tasks for the day

They are very accommodating, and there are usually multiple types of tasks available if you have any limitations.

***

## **Important Details (Please Read)**

### Location

MANNA FoodBank
99 Broadpointe Drive, Mills River, NC
*Doors open 10 minutes before the shift — **please arrive a 15 minutes early**.*

### Liability Waiver

* Waivers will be provided **on-site**
* All volunteers must sign upon arrival
* Volunteers 17 and under require a parent or guardian signature

### Dress Code

* **Closed-toe shoes are required** (no exceptions)
* Wear comfortable clothes you don’t mind getting a little dirty

### What to Bring

* Water or your preferred beverage
* Light snacks will be available

### Guidelines

To maintain a safe and welcoming environment:

* **Nicotine-Free Facility**
* No smoking, vaping, or nicotine use inside or within fenced areas
* Items must be stored in your vehicle
* Designated smoking area is at the far end of the parking lot
* **Substance-Free Workplace**
* No alcohol, drugs, or impairing substances (including THC/Kratom)
* **Age Requirement**
* Volunteers must be **10 years or older**

This is a great opportunity to connect with the AVL Digital Nomads community while giving back in a meaningful way.
Come be part of it

title: Four-Hand Piano Trio
location: NC
description:
AmiciMusic continues their Music at the Museum series with a program entitled Four-Hand Piano Trio on Thursday, April 30 at 6:30pm. 
The concert features an international ensemble of musicians—Vadim Tchikil, violin (from France/Russia), Jacques-Pierre Malan, cello (from South Africa), Francesco Cipolletta, piano (from Italy), and pianist/artistic director Daniel Weiser. 
They will perform a program featuring exciting music for violin, cello, and four-hand piano, a very rare and unique combination.  They will play two of the four quartets by Romantic composer Hermann Berens for this combination, as well as some spirited arrangements of the Brahms Hungarian Dances and Liszt’s Rhapsody no. 2. 
AmiciMusic is an award-winning non-profit chamber music organization dedicated to performing intimate, high-quality concerts in non-traditional spaces and to breaking down barriers between performers and audiences through fun, informative talks before each piece is played.  It should be a spectacular show you will not want to miss! 
Purchase Tickets 
  
The Steinway piano is available to the Asheville Art Museum through the courtesy of the Asheville Chamber Music Series.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Updated: The Biltmore Farm Trail Is Fairly Flat and a 6 Mile Round Trip—Join Us!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
**Update: The Farm Trail and the Arbor Trace Trail are currently closed (as of March 8). If still closed on May 2, we will walk the Lagoon Trail instead. The start point in the same, but the distance is shorter.**

In front of the Antler Hill Barn, by the Playground, there is a picnic shelter known as the Antler Hill Pavillion. We will meet there at 9:30 a.m.

We will walk the seldom-done Farm Trail along the French Broad River edge of the estate property, mostly out and back. Biltmore says it is a 6-mile (10 KM) round trip.

Dress for the weather. Bring a protein snack and water. Walking sticks only if you want them since the walk will be mostly level. Tennis shoes should be okay, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case light hiking boots would be better. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should work ok.

You will need a grounds pass, so arrive no later than 9 a.m. to purchase it and let me know so we will wait to start the walk until you have joined us. We actually recommend the purchase of an annual pass, as we will be walking on the estate grounds several times in the coming year.

Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-2nd-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[CLICK HERE TO PURCHASE YOU TICKET AND RESERVE YOUR SPACE FOR THIS EVENT.](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-2nd-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-2nd-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)

**What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?**
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

* 6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle
* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
* 8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
* 11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision. ](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.
