title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles! We will either be in the large room inside or out back on the patio depending on weather.

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. Feel free to share as much or as little as you want! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club!
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**May Selection - *Beautiful Country: A Memoir of an Undocumented Childhood* by Qian Julie Wang**

In Chinese, the word for America, Mei Guo, translates directly to “beautiful country.” Yet when seven-year-old Qian arrives in New York City in 1994 full of curiosity, she is overwhelmed by crushing fear and scarcity. In China, Qian’s parents were professors; in America, her family is “illegal” and it will require all the determination and small joys they can muster to survive. Inhabiting her childhood perspective with exquisite lyric clarity and unforgettable charm and strength, Qian Julie Wang has penned an essential American story about a family fracturing under the weight of invisibility, and a girl coming of age in the shadows, who never stops seeking the light.

**Welcome** to our robust and engaging Book Club! We're a small, friendly group dedicated to fostering lively discussions about our monthly book selections. Whether you've read the entire book, just a few chapters, or even if you're simply curious about the title, we'd love to have you join us!

**Meeting Schedule**: We gather on the First Tuesday of every month for our book discussions.

What sets us apart is our small group size and directed discussions. This intimate setting allows for deeper, more engaging conversations where everyone's voice can be heard. It's the perfect environment for those who love to dive deep into themes, characters, and the intricacies of storytelling.

So whether you're a seasoned bookworm or just dipping your toes into the world of literature, we invite you to join us. Let's explore new worlds, challenge our perspectives, and forge new friendships - one book at a time!

title: AVL UX - A First “get to know” the UX community
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
AVL UX (hosted by AVL Digital Nomads) is Asheville’s new meetup for UX, product, and research folks. This first event is casual and low-pressure and focuses on- quick intros, small-group chats, and a short “what should we do next?” moment.

What if Asheville had a regular place where UX people could actually find each other and it without, feeling like a stiff “networking event”? **AVL UX is Asheville’s new meetup for UX, product, and research meant to build and connect the local community to shape what the**
**UX scene here becomes.**

This first gathering is intentionally **friendly + low-pressure**. Come as you are: working designer, researcher, PM, engineer, student, career-switcher, or just UX-curious. The goal is simple: meet people, trade notes, and leave with new connections (and a clearer idea of what AVL UX should be next).

**What to expect**

* Quick welcomes + name tags (so it’s easy to meet people).
* Casual small-group conversations and prompts (And hopefully no awkward interactions).
* A short “what should AVL UX do next?” moment (talks, portfolio nights, design jams, a Config watch party 2026, etc.)

**A few topics up for discussion**

* **What’s your Asheville UX Scene?:** Where is everyone and what is everyone doing in Asheville? Why UX here as the industry is rather small
* **Design-to-code + vibe-coding workflows:** what’s actually working with tools like Figma Make/MCP + Cursor—and what breaks in real teams?
* **Accessibility is becoming the baseline:** how are you baking WCAG 2.2 into design + dev early (instead of last-minute fixes)?
* **Design systems + tokens in 2026:** how do we keep tokens clean, scalable, and synced between design + code without “token rot”?
* **Calm, mindful UX:** how do we reduce cognitive load and create more “human” experiences instead of noisy, attention-grabby UI?

For our first meeting we’ll go to Hi-Wire Brewing in RAD. Easy to get to with plenty of parking. A great assortment of both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. Typically there is a food truck as well.

Looking forward to meeting everyone and launching our new UX community!

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Raphael Revealed
location: NC
description:
Marking the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death, the greatest exhibition ever held of his works took place in Rome. Exhibition on Screen was granted exclusive access to this once-in-a-lifetime show. With over two hundred masterpieces, including paintings and drawings – over a hundred of which have been brought together for the first time – this major exhibition celebrates the life and work of Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino. 
With unprecedented loans from the Louvre, Uffizi, National Gallery of Art, the Prado Museum and more, the exhibition and this film provide an unprecedented opportunity to see the breadth of Raphael’s skill, creativity and ingenuity. Award-winning director Phil Grabsky provides a fresh look at this giant of the Renaissance, and shows why he is considered one of the all-time greats. The film covers his life in Rome, and includes unique footage of the ancient Rome that was such a powerful influence, including rare footage of Nero’s Golden House that Raphael himself visited. 
More than just a painter, Raphael was one of the most extraordinary artists of the Renaissance but is often misunderstood or mythologised. On the basis of this extraordinary exhibition in Rome, this film allows Raphael, for the first time, to be truly revealed. Directed by Phil Grabsky. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Mother's Day Walk in Waynesville from Mast General to Middle School & Back
description:

Bring your mother, or anyone else, or come alone. Let's do a Mother's Day walk in Waynesville.

Meet at 2:00 in front of Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. We will meet at the rocking chairs in front of the door to the shoe department.

The walk goes past public art, to Frog Level for a brief stop at Panacea Coffee Company, to Waynesville Middle School, through an interesting neighborhood, and back to the start point.

There are some hills, so some may want a walking pole; sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen.

Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it. There are one or two restrooms along the route.

title: AI Hacks and Hops - From Chatbot to Co-Worker: AI for Business
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**From Chatbot to Co-Worker: A Business Guide to AI That Actually Works**
**Speaker:** [Julio Barros](https://www.linkedin.com/in/juliobarros/)

**Description:** Most business owners use AI the way people used the internet in 1996, they check the weather. They type questions into ChatGPT, read the answer, and close the tab. Meanwhile, a quiet revolution is underway: small teams are using AI agents to run real business operations, following up with leads, generating reports, managing content pipelines, and handling customer support autonomously.
The gap between "asking AI questions" and "giving AI a job" is the biggest competitive window most of us will see in our careers. But closing that gap wrong is worse than not closing it at all.
This session walks you through the progression from chatbot to co-worker with live demonstrations, then gives you a practical framework for identifying where to start in your own business - and what order to do it in so you don't automate the wrong thing first.

**General Event Info**
AI Hacks and Hops is a monthly event tailored for non-technical professionals, entrepreneurs, marketers, engineers, or anyone who wants to explore and discuss how to use AI.

Each gathering will feature presentations, stimulating group discussions, and a relaxed atmosphere for enjoying your favorite brews while delving into the world of AI. Topics will range from AI integration in business processes, marketing, content creation, software, ethical considerations, human-AI collaboration strategies, to the latest advancements in AI technology. The informal setting encourages open dialogue, idea exchange, and fosters a collaborative spirit.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Psychedelic Integration Circle
description:
Psychedelic Society of Asheville
We invite you to gather with us in a safe, confidential, and supportive space to share, reflect, and connect with community.

Integration is a practice of intentionally slowing down, listening inward, and making meaning of our experiences so they can truly support and enrich our lives. Through integration, we can cultivate greater awareness of our thoughts, emotions, and patterns, allowing us to move through life’s changes with greater resilience, clarity, and compassion.

We are delighted to welcome Becca Marshall as our Psychedelic Integration Circle facilitator. Becca is an Integrative Psychotherapist, Aligned Living Coach, Psychedelic Integration Guide, and the founder of ActivXchange. Her work supports individuals navigating major life transitions, whether entering adulthood, stepping into leadership, or guiding others through healing and transformation, with grounded presence and deep care.

This ongoing circle is open to all whether you are simply curious, actively preparing for or integrating psychedelic experiences, or have been walking this path for some time. Our intention is to foster connection, shared wisdom, and mutual support within our ever-growing psychedelic community here in Asheville. All are welcome.

Please note that this is a sober gathering. To ensure the integrity and safety of our space, we do not permit the sale, purchase, or sourcing of any illegal substances or activities at our events. Anyone not honoring these guidelines will be respectfully asked to leave.

This gathering is offered with a suggested $10 donation. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. Contributions help cover venue costs and support future offerings from the Psychedelic Society of Asheville.

Thank you for being part of this community and we look forward to gathering with you soon! ✨

title: Downtown Asheville Scavenger Hunt 2.0
description:
Friendly People in Asheville
It’s spring, y’all, so it’s time for **Downtown Asheville Scavenger Hunt 2.0**. 🎉

Same fun hunt, all new clues. Whether you joined our hunt last fall or are brand new to the game, come out and give it a try! This is a fun way to explore Asheville and make new friends.

Here’s how it works:

We will gather at the S&W Market at 56 Patton Avenue at 2:30pm. We’ll hang out upstairs — at Periscope — and get snacks and drinks, etc. If you’re a little late, no worries.

We will break up into teams and go over the rules at 3:15pm. Teams will have 10-15 minutes to review the clues, and the hunt will begin at 3:30pm.

Teams will have an hour to hunt for 40 clues scattered across downtown and take a selfie with each clue. \*Bonus points for taking a selfie with the clue and a willing stranger. More willing strangers = more points.\*

The hunt ends at 4:30pm back at Periscope in the S&W.

It will take 20-30 minutes to review all the teams’ answers and determine the winner.
The prize will be the glory of winning! 🏆
That said, this hunt’s 40th question is a diabolical bonus question with only one correct answer. Get it right, and I’ll buy you (and everyone on your team) a drink.

**What to bring:**

* Walking or running shoes (the hunt spans from South Slope to the north end of downtown)
* Your phone for taking pics
* A pencil or pen to mark off clues as you find them
* Your competitive spirit!

**Parking:**
Parking is available nearby at the Rankin (68 Rankin Ave) and Wall Street (45 Wall Street) parking decks, as well as at the Coxe Ave Garage (52 Coxe Ave). Metered street parking is also available around the corner on Church Street.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**
Participants are responsible for their safety. If you sign up or participate in this event, you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event.

Looking forward to seeing y’all there!

Three laps on the Bobcat Trail amounts to 3.1 miles. Bobcat consists of both natural and paved surfaces. There is a little elevation change on the route, but nothing too strenuous.

We will stop to look at a different garden on each counterclockwise lap. The first lap we will stop at the Bird and Butterfly Garden. The second lap we will stop at the Dahlia Garden. The third lap we will stop at the Rhododendron Garden. All three should be in beautiful bloom. Bring your camera!

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. Consider sunscreen and a hat. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring my walking sticks.

As always, you are urged to bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have much problem. There are no bathrooms available that afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Third Thursday featuring Jackson Grimm and Clint Roberts of Holler Choir
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
This month Asheville-based, nationally recognized musicians Jackson Grimm and Clint Roberts will play in the Museum’s Atrium from 6-8pm. Grimm and Roberts, who also play in popular band Holler Choir, bring together old time, swing band music with indie rock creating a unique and satisfying sound. Sit and listen for a while, grab a drink from our Perspectives Cafe pop up bar, and then take some time to stroll the galleries and discover your favorite artworks at night! And don’t forgot to stop by the Studio and silkscreen yourself a poster to take home! 
Jackson Grimm is an accomplished and respected band leader, multi-instrumentalist and teacher in the Western North Carolina music community. His songs marry folk pop melodies with the lonesome sound of traditional Appalachian music. In a region with a strong music culture, it is no surprise that Grimm’s songwriting is representative of his musical birthplace: Asheville, NC. 
Grimm won the 2025 LEAF Songwriting competition and has been a 2 year finalist for the Songwriter Serenade. He has shared the stage with and opened up for acts such as Molly Tuttle, Sierra Ferrell, Shadowgrass, the Wilder Flower, Arlo Guthrie, Tim Grimm, Ben Bedford, Ordinary Elephant, Nathan Evans Fox, and more.” 
Clint Roberts was raised in the Appalachian mountains of Western North Carolina and crafts songs that bridge the gap between the region’s deep-rooted folk traditions and the contemporary Americana heard on national airwaves. After dedicating a decade to his solo singer-songwriter career beginning in his early twenties, Clint founded the collective-driven string band Holler Choir in Asheville, NC, in 2021. 
Since then, Holler Choir has toured extensively across the United States and expanded its creative reach by becoming the backing band for a second project, the Susto String Band, formed in collaboration with the band Susto. In 2024, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Jackson Grimm joined both Holler Choir and the Susto String Band and now co-leads the project alongside Clint.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: May 23rd Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-23rd-community-cuddles)**[Click HERE to register!](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-23rd-community-cuddles)**

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**
1\. Clothes stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\.
4\. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with\.
5\. Speak up if you have a question\, concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. All emotions are welcome\- we love vulnerability\.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.
* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Raphael Revealed
location: NC
description:
Marking the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death, the greatest exhibition ever held of his works took place in Rome. Exhibition on Screen was granted exclusive access to this once-in-a-lifetime show. With over two hundred masterpieces, including paintings and drawings – over a hundred of which have been brought together for the first time – this major exhibition celebrates the life and work of Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino. 
With unprecedented loans from the Louvre, Uffizi, National Gallery of Art, the Prado Museum and more, the exhibition and this film provide an unprecedented opportunity to see the breadth of Raphael’s skill, creativity and ingenuity. Award-winning director Phil Grabsky provides a fresh look at this giant of the Renaissance, and shows why he is considered one of the all-time greats. The film covers his life in Rome, and includes unique footage of the ancient Rome that was such a powerful influence, including rare footage of Nero’s Golden House that Raphael himself visited. 
More than just a painter, Raphael was one of the most extraordinary artists of the Renaissance but is often misunderstood or mythologised. On the basis of this extraordinary exhibition in Rome, this film allows Raphael, for the first time, to be truly revealed. Directed by Phil Grabsky.

title: Holiday Weekend Sunday Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
What better way to spend the Sunday afternoon before Memorial Day than by walking with a meetup group?

Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 clockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: May 29th An Evening of Spicy/Sensual Snuggles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-29th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[CLICK HERE TO PURCHASE YOU TICKET AND RESERVE YOUR SPACE FOR THIS EVENT.](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-29th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-29th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)

**What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?**
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

* 6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle
* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
* 8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
* 11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision. ](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.
\*Refund Policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Take a walking tour of the city of Brevard. We will meet at 9:00. This walk will be 5 KM (3 miles).

title: Adult Studio: Landscape // Wild and Free
location: NC
description:
Join instructor Ehren Fritz Gerhard in this three-hour session of plein air painting on location at Zealandia Estate! Students will interpret the landscape using a combination of abstract and realistic painting techniques. Learn how to utilize a limited color palette and limited brushes to emphasize the fundamental structure of your paintings. Minimalism in the landscape, expressive color palettes, bold brushstrokes, and visual contrast will be the primary focus of this session accompanied by instructor demonstration, guidance, and group critique. 
Ehren Fritz Gerhard completed his Master of Fine Arts from Arizona State University in 2013 and Bachelor of Arts from Florida Gulf Coast University in 2009.  He has been an Adjunct Professor of Drawing and Printmaking at Florida Gulf Coast University as well as Basic Design and Color Theory at Florida Southwestern State College. He lives in Asheville, North Carolina with his wife, daughter, son, and dog where he maintains an active studio, works on his garden and goes on primitive camping and fishing trips as often as possible. 
REGISTER HERE

title: Bonsai Update: Walking the Forest Meadow at the NC Arboretum
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
**Bonsai Update: The Bonsai in the Blue Ridge ticketed event will be going on June 4 – 7. You very well may want to stay after the walk for lunch and the Bonsai event. Plan accordingly.**

Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center at 09:30 a.m. Restrooms are available at the start point.

We will walk through the Formal Gardens and the Bonsai Exhibit. Then we will make our way to the Forest Meadow, walking around all the paths. We'll go down Running Cedar Road, across on Bent Creek Road (taking the Creekside Trails), and return on Wesley Branch Road.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Some may want walking poles. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring plenty of water and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome, but are not allowed in buildings or the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $20 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend for the driver to purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: Body Process Class: Circuitry
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
## What If Your Body Has Been Waiting for This?

## **You’re Invited: Access Consciousness Body Process Class**

What if your body isn’t something to fix…
but something to listen to?

What if it has been whispering (or maybe shouting) for your attention in ways you were never taught to understand?

I’d love to invite you to a beautiful, hands-on **Access Consciousness Body Process class** — a space where you get to receive, gift, and explore a different communion with bodies.

### What Is a Body Process?

Access Consciousness Body Processes are gentle, hands-on techniques that invite the body to:
• Release stored trauma and shock
• Activate natural capacities
• Undo limitations held in tissue and cellular memory
• Restore communication between you and your body

This isn’t massage.
It isn’t energy work in the traditional sense.
It’s a conversation — with the body.
And bodies respond.

### In This Class You Will:

✨ Learn a specific Access Body Process you can use for life
✨ Both gift and receive the process (yes, you get sessions too!)
✨ Explore how judgment impacts the body
✨ Discover new tools for ease, vitality, and awareness
✨ Leave certified to practice this body process on others

No prior experience is required. Just a body. And a willingness.

### What Becomes Possible?

Many people report:
• Increased ease in chronic patterns
• Greater relaxation and presence
• Changes in long-held physical limitations
• A deeper sense of trust with their body

But more than anything — possibility.
What if your body has capacities you’ve never been shown how to access?

Spots are limited only by space - the sooner you sign up the sooner we can look for larger locations if required.

If you’ve been asking for more ease, more connection, more *aliveness* — this may be the invitation your body has been waiting for.

Would your body enjoy this?
